data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2019 gross claims outstanding were $2,734.141m. During 2019 there was a gross prior-year strengthening of $156.605m (an increase in gross claims provisions) as disclosed in the technical provisions movement; however a larger increase in reinsurers' recoveries produced a net release of $34.847m. The movements relate primarily to property catastrophe activity and associated reinsurance recoveries following a series of natural catastrophe events (notably 2017 and 2018 hurricanes, typhoons and California wildfires) and adjustments to reinsurance recoverables.
raw_causal_phrases: Over/under-provision in respect of prior claims and claim adjustment expenses 156,605 (191,452) (34,847)
There was a release of $23.1 million from the closed years of 2016 and prior representing approximately 3.1% of RITC brought forward at constant exchange rates.
The 2017 account picked up almost all of the reinsurance loss from the 2017 hurricanes (Harvey, Irma, Maria) together with a share of direct property loss.

The 2018 account will pick up almost all of the reinsurance loss from the 2018 hurricanes (Florence, Michael), typhoons (Jebi, Trami) and Californian wildfire losses together with a share of the direct property loss from these events.

The 2019 account will pick up almost all of the reinsurance loss from the 2019 hurricane (Dorian) and typhoons (Faxai and Hagibis) together with a share of the direct property loss on Hurricane Dorian.

data.data_quality_notes: All monetary figures are reported in the syndicate's functional/presentation currency (USD). Opening reserves and prior-year movement are taken from the technical provisions note: the gross 'Over/under-provision in respect of prior claims and claim adjustment expenses' (gross column) is used as the prior year development (explicit gross number). The net effect is different (net release) because reinsurers' share increased. Some causal attributions (e.g. link to particular catastrophe events) are inferred from narrative; amounts for individual events are not quantified in the source and are therefore null. Claims development triangle is available (gross) and was used as secondary validation.
